case.title: Wexmoor: a pay rise for care workers while the national deal is awaited
case.question: Should Wexmoor use its care fund to add a flat pay rise for every care worker on its contracts, or to give long-serving staff a bonus?
case.story: Wexmoor is a made-up county council that buys home care from 14 small firms. About 1,400 care workers are paid close to the minimum wage, and the firms say they lose someone every few weeks to shops and warehouses. The council has set aside 2.4 million pounds a year for two years, from April 2027, to bridge the gap until a national pay deal arrives. A flat extra 1 pound an hour for every contracted care worker would cost about 1.9 million pounds a year with employer costs. A bonus for staff with long service would cost less, but leave newer and part-time staff out. Firms, unions and families all say they want the money in pay packets and the visits to carry on.

in_the_news.headline: New Chair to lead landmark care worker pay talks
in_the_news.why: England's first sector-wide pay talks for care workers will not settle until April 2028, so a made-up council has to decide what to do for its care workers in the meantime.

facts.text: The first Fair Pay Agreement for adult social care in England is backed by 500 million pounds and covers 1.5 million people.
Negotiations start in April 2027, and the first settlement is due to be introduced by April 2028.

sources.title: New Chair to lead landmark care worker pay talks
sources.publisher: Department of Health and Social Care

tests.text: Says every care worker on a council contract gets the rise, part-time and zero-hours included.
Says how the council checks the money reaches pay slips, and who does the checking.
Names one owner for the scheme and a start date of April 2027.
Says what happens to the rise when the national pay deal arrives in 2028.
Must not cost more than 2.4 million pounds a year.
Must not cut the hours of care the council buys, or take money from other care budgets.

voices.who: a man, 40s, West Midlands, private rent
voices.text: Give it to everyone on the contract, not just the ones who have been there longest. The new starters are the ones who leave first, so a bonus for stayers does nothing for them.

voices.who: a woman, 20s, South East, social housing
voices.text: A flat hour on every pay slip, in writing, with a start date. If I can't see it on my payslip in April, I'll know nobody checked.
Check it actually reaches the carers. Last time the money went to the firm and the firm kept it. Name someone at the council who answers for it.

voices.who: a man, 40s, North West, long-term sick
voices.text: Carers on zero hours need the rise too. And don't cut my visits to pay for it. I need the same care every week.

bench.angle: Flat 1 pound an hour rise written into every contract
bench.title: A flat extra pound an hour, in every contract, checked on pay slips
bench.answer: From April 2027 Wexmoor adds 1 pound an hour to every care worker on its contracts, part-time and zero-hours included,. The Director of Adult Social Care owns it. Firms send payroll records monthly; council finance checks a sample against pay slips and withholds payment from any firm that cannot show the rise reached workers. It costs about 1.9 million pounds a year, inside the 2.4 million fund, the rest kept for checking and a reserve. No visits are cut and no other care budget is touched. When the national deal arrives in 2028, the rise counts towards it, so nobody loses it and the council never pays twice. It worked if staff leaving falls against last year.

bench.angle: Loyalty bonus for long-serving care staff only
bench.title: A yearly loyalty bonus for care staff with two years' service
bench.answer: Wexmoor pays a yearly bonus of 900 pounds, in April from 2027, to every care worker with two or more years of service with a council-contracted firm. The council's care commissioning team runs it, using lists of staff that the firms send in. It costs about 1.1 million pounds a year from the care fund, so the rest stays unspent. Visits and other care budgets are left alone. Newer staff and many part-time workers would get nothing, and the answer sets no pay slip check beyond the firms' own lists. It does not say what happens when the national deal starts. We would know it worked if more long-serving staff stay.

bench.angle: Rise plus a paid-training and guaranteed-hours offer
bench.title: Raise care pay, train on paid time, offer secure hours
bench.answer: From April 2027, Wexmoor’s care director owns a contractual £1 hourly rise for every contracted carer, including part-time and zero-hours staff. The dedicated fund pays £1.9m annually. Within the remaining £500,000, firms offer paid training and voluntary guaranteed hours matching existing working patterns; checking and cover come first. Total spending stays below £2.4m annually, with no cuts to purchased care hours or other care budgets. Council payroll auditors check monthly payslips against hours worked and require missing pay repaid. Publish payment coverage, missed visits and staff departures quarterly. Fold the rise into the 2028 national deal without reducing hourly pay. Review training and retention after twelve months; extra funding ends March 2029 unless renewed.

gate.verdict: Answer A and answer C meet every test and limit. Answer B leaves out newer and part-time staff, has no pay slip check and is silent on the 2028 deal, though it keeps within both limits.
